tree_state: all files listed under sha256 except task.json were uncommitted at recording time and are committed in the commit that follows this record; the recorded commit is its parent
summary: A static ad-hoc signed arm64 Mach-O probe (16635 bytes) that reads /dev/rmd1 in 128 KiB chunks and prints a SHA-256 with prefix digests every 128 MiB, built with the project toolchain (NDK clang 18.0.2 + LLD + mkstatic.py); its own FIPS 180-4 SHA-256; a padder that makes the 2,475,712,512-byte donor root image 2,475,720,704 bytes (a 16 KiB multiple) and records both digests; 108 tests (21 need Unicorn); a mutation pass of 1311 candidates (1184 valid, 1131 killed, 53 survivors, each examined and recorded as equivalent with a reason); and a decision draft for NAT-078. Nothing was run on the phone; the Mach-O was executed only under Unicorn with a fake six-syscall kernel.

acceptance.1_probe: src/hash-probe.c + src/sha256.h, built by build.py into artifacts/nat-077/build-final2/hash-probe (16635 bytes, sha256 dc5c7845b3856274b0c8b5519f5b2a726c595de5410cb6cfa818fe0645a258b7). It reads the device in 131072-byte chunks, prints digest, byte count and seconds, and progress lines. SHA-256 is an own implementation of FIPS 180-4 (no third-party code; see deviations). The same C file built for the host (-DHOST_TEST) gives hashlib's digest for FIPS vectors, lengths 1-299, chunk boundaries, short reads, EINTR, a 513 MiB sparse input, and the real padded image (artifacts/nat-077/logs/host-digest-padded.txt). The final Mach-O is run under Unicorn (probe_vm.py) and produces the same digests and exit status 81.
acceptance.2_builder: pad_root.py pads 2475712512 bytes to 2475720704 bytes (151106 pages of 16 KiB) with zeros, verifies size and read-back, refuses a size that is not a multiple of its unit (default 16384; a 4096 unit is accepted, anything not a multiple of 4096 is refused), and records source and padded SHA-256 in artifacts/nat-077/padded.json (6304b2c54d56055e8df7b2b63dcbe79a9415d860b598cb8e11bda5eed47e150f -> 552800ff3ac3de129b550c838681d0cb1d08cc4df0d38b2dc1088a9b258a8258). The Apple-derived image stays in artifacts/ (gitignored); only sizes and hashes are committed.
acceptance.3_decision_draft: docs/procedures/nat-077/decision-draft.md: question, observables (device-committed offset, rate, prefix and final digests, page size, ending), budgets, an 8-row pass table fixed beforehand, deviations from the registry text. Nothing was run on the phone.

findings: LLD's darwin flavour ignores -static and places __text at 0x4000, so mkinit.py (one position-independent __text) cannot take compiled C directly; mkstatic.py shifts the sections by a multiple of 4 KiB and rebuilds the segments, load commands and CodeDirectory. A header comparison shows the new Mach-O has the same segments and load commands as the NAT-075 probe that did boot as PID 1 (both 16635 bytes), differing only in four __TEXT sections instead of one.
A writable global made LLD emit __DATA,__data, which the wrapper refuses; the probe keeps all state on the stack.

The first version of the unreadable-device test hung (300 s): with fd 3 closed, /dev/fd/1 opened as fd 3 and the probe read the console pipe. The test now uses a second host build with a nonexistent device path.
pad_root.py would have unlinked a destination it did not create if opening it exclusively failed; fixed (it now unlinks only a file it created) and tested.

Mutation passes found real test gaps, each closed with a test and re-run: the first pass left 210 unexplained survivors (the fake kernel numbered descriptors from 3 only, the Unicorn stack was zero-filled, the wrapper's refusals and the padder's fallback paths were untested); the second left 66, of which the dylib-command constants, a section segment name of 16 characters, a device handed descriptor 0 and the real-clock path (a 0.4 s stall test that killed a seconds-only clock by chance, now 1.25 s plus a non-round-milliseconds check) were gaps; the third pass has 53 survivors, all examined, all equivalent (equivalent.json, mutation.json).
Descriptor numbering: whether the payload kernel hands PID 1 stdio descriptors is not established; the probe works with the console as descriptor 0, as 3, and with the device as descriptor 0.

The mutation runner leaked host-probe grandchildren of mutants that hung the tests (four were found running and killed by PID); it now runs every test pass in its own session and kills the process group on a timeout (checked).
established: Host-test: the probe's C code computes SHA-256 correctly in the cases listed in acceptance 1 and prints the documented text and exit codes in each error case (0x60-0x63, 81).

Host-test: the final signed Mach-O parses with an independent Mach-O/CodeDirectory reader in the tests, runs under Unicorn from _start with a 16-byte-aligned and a misaligned stack, issues only exit/read/write/open/getpid/gettimeofday with the Darwin register and carry-flag convention, and prints the same digests as hashlib.
Host-test: the padder and the wrapper refuse the listed bad inputs; the padded image has the recorded size and digest; a host build of the probe over it prints the same digest.
Host-test: a mutation pass over sha256.h, hash-probe.c, mkstatic.py and pad_root.py (1184 valid mutants, 1131 killed, 53 survivors, 0 unexplained) shows the tests notice changes to those files.
not_established: Anything about the S24: that the payload kernel starts this Mach-O (the NAT-075 probe with the same header and segments did), that gettimeofday returns usable time there, how /dev/rmd1 behaves under read(2) (alignment, short reads), and how fast the device hashes (scalar C).
Any byte in md1, the host-to-phone USB rate, U5 and watchdog feeding while the loader serves bulk transfers (NAT-078, NAT-071).
That the Unicorn kernel model is faithful to XNU: it is a few dozen lines written for these tests.
That the mutation pass covers the arm64-only paths beyond what Unicorn executes; the mutation generators do not delete single terms of a condition.

deviations_from_task_text: Acceptance 1 says the SHA-256 is 'an included public-domain or permissively licensed implementation'. The implementation is written from FIPS 180-4 for this task; there is no third-party code to include, license or attribute. Correctness rests on the tests (FIPS vectors, hashlib agreement).
The Mach-O is produced by NDK clang + LLD + mkstatic.py, not by mkinit.py alone: mkinit.py takes one position-independent __text and C needs a linker.

The registry has no command to extend NAT-078's dependency list. The two prerequisites this task's results show to be necessary (NAT-079: the delivery loader; NAT-080: the session driver and analyser) were registered as separate host tasks and are named as preconditions in decision-draft.md section 8; NAT-078 must not be claimed before both are done.

'Seconds' in the probe output are wall-clock seconds from gettimeofday, because the Darwin ABI offers no cheaper clock to a freestanding program; whether it advances at that point of the boot is for NAT-078 to see.
